prompts.core:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: authored pixel-art boss animation sheet for a 2D side-scrolling Metal Gear fan game. Make a NEW original square 1024x1024 image containing exactly 4 columns x 4 rows, 16 equal cells. Absolutely flat chroma magenta #ff00ff background. Exactly five thin cyan vertical grid lines and five thin cyan horizontal grid lines, including outer borders, equally spaced. No words, numbers, captions, labels, watermark, scenery, base, ground shadows or other actors.
Subject: METAL GEAR D from Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake, the 1990 MSX2 machine designed by Tomohiro Nishio, not Metal Gear REX, not TX-55, not ZEKE, not Sahelanthropus. The recognisable D silhouette is a squat bulky olive/blue-green military tank cockpit BODY directly above two articulated mechanical legs. No separate animal neck or dinosaur head; NO HUMANOID ARMS OR HANDS. Dense rounded/faceted cast-metal central armored hull, raised circular sensor lenses/domes, small front optical lens cluster and searchlight, thin radio antennae; a large tall rectangular SIX-PORT missile pod high at the rear/shoulder, and a projecting multi-barrel ROTARY CANNON fixed beside the front hull. Two thick upper leg assemblies with prominent hydraulic pistons and exposed hoses, bent mechanical knee geometry, narrower elongated lower-leg rods and armor; broad mechanical feet with TWO pointed front toes plus a rear heel spur. Paint is muted desaturated military teal/olive-green, gunmetal hardware and black rubber hoses, restrained worn edges and tiny amber/red optical accents. This is an early practical utilitarian military walker, not an elegant futuristic humanoid robot. NO spherical or dish radar, NO huge REX railgun, NO flipper wings, NO sword or human fists. Keep the mounted cannon and missile pod visible and consistent in all frames.
Style: crisp detailed 16-bit/32-bit PIXEL ART with deliberate visible pixel clusters, dark outline and limited palette, not a photograph or 3D render. Fixed orthographic SIDE VIEW every frame faces SCREEN RIGHT. Slight offset of far leg so exactly two legs remain readable, no front/three-quarter view and no camera rotation. All sixteen cells have the same body scale, common virtual ground baseline y=228, whole machine visible with at least 24px empty margin on every edge. Standing height approximately 190px. Antenna tips and weapon barrels must never cross a cyan line.
ROW1 IDLE: four distinct subtle weight-balancing/servo poses; cockpit and cannon shift slightly, tiny sensor intensity changes, feet stay planted. ROW2 MOVE: four real slow walking poses, near leg reaches forward, weight passes, far leg advances, weight passes opposite; mechanical knees and pistons noticeably articulate. ROW3 CHARGE: four firing preparations; spread feet, lower center of mass, angle cannon straight RIGHT, open missile pod ports/ready cannon. ROW4 ATTACK: four distinct weapon firing phases: short amber muzzle flash from the rotary cannon, recoil slight hull kick, single small missile nose leaving the six-port launcher, cannon finishes burst and smoke dissipates. No huge explosion, no long projectile trail, no laser beam. Keep flash/missile within 15px of the muzzle and within the cell; actual gameplay projectiles are separate. Exactly one intact D per cell, sixteen distinct purposeful poses, no decorative background objects.
prompts.coreAnatomyCorrection: Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct ONLY the leg and foot anatomy in this Metal Gear D sprite atlas to make it more faithful to the MG2 machine, while preserving the same exact green hull, six-port rectangular missile pod, rotary cannon, sensors, antennae, colors, RIGHT-facing orthographic side view, all 16 animation actions, 4x4 grid, flat magenta and cyan guidelines. The D needs longer industrial mechanical legs: heavy upper knee housings, clearly visible long paired hydraulic piston shafts below the knees and long narrow shin armor, not short humanoid robot calves. Legs from underside of hull to foot soles should make up about 55 percent of the complete standing machine height excluding antennas and tall missile box. Achieve this within the SAME TOTAL standing height and ground baseline by slightly shortening the hull vertically, never clipping any cell. Give each foot exactly TWO long pointed forward toes and a small rear heel spur, not three human-like toes or broad boots. Keep all other hardware and both weapons identical, no new equipment and no humanoid arms. Keep identical scale across all cells and at least 20px clean magenta inside every edge. The cannon remains on the front of the HULL, no separate arm or human hand. Do not modify the animation sequence, final attack muzzle flashes remain compact and in-cell. One precise mechanical-anatomy correction only.
prompts.coreWalkCorrection: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit ONLY the SECOND ROW (four cells of the walking animation) of this Metal Gear D atlas. Preserve ALL pixels in rows 1, 3 and 4, background, grid, scale and the exact machine anatomy and colors. Maintain the longer piston lower legs, two-toed feet, compact green hull and six-port missile launcher + front rotary cannon identically. Fixed orthographic RIGHT side view, no front view. Whole actor remains fully contained with >=20px magenta margin, same ground baseline and same height/scale. Do not change the machine into a humanoid. No new text or decorations. Only repair walking motion in row2.
prompts.special:
Use case: identity-preserve. Edit this Metal Gear D CORE atlas into its companion SPECIAL atlas. Image1 is the exact approved subject/style/anatomy reference. Keep the same compact olive teal tank hull, front rotary cannon, tall SIX-port missile pod, sensors and antennas, long paired hydraulic lower leg pistons and TWO pointed front toes on each foot. No human arms, no head/neck separate from hull, no REX railgun or radar, no wings. Maintain the identical 4x4 square grid, exactly FIVE thin cyan vertical and FIVE horizontal lines, flat solid #ff00ff magenta background with no texture. No text, labels, numbering, UI, scenery or cast shadow. All16 cells face SCREEN RIGHT with fixed orthographic side view, same actor scale and same common foot baseline as the core. Entire actor, gun and antenna tips have >=24 pixels magenta clearance from all borders. Standing scan poses must be exactly same height as core idle.
Replace all poses with these four animation rows left to right. ROW1 RECOVER: four phases following cannon/missile fire, crouched braced stance with barrel recoil, cannon slides forward as hull rises, legs straighten and stabilise, return to idle. ROW2 HIT: four distinct impact reactions, hull jolts back/up a few degrees with tiny LOCAL amber sparks on armor, near knee flexes, hull leans and legs rebalance, regain controlled stance. Keep attached weapons and no big particle explosion. ROW3 DEATH: first knees buckle and forward hull dips; second rests kneeling with cannon pointing slightly down; third hull collapses to the floor supported by folded legs, missile pod tilted but still attached; fourth definitive inert low wreck lying with long legs folded under/behind, barrel low, optics DARK and antennas bent, no subsequent revival. Do not scatter detached pieces outside cell and do not obscure actor in smoke. ROW4 SCAN: four active standing idle scan phases, sensors pulse amber/green and front hull pivots subtly up/level/down/level, feet planted and no weapons firing. This row is independent, not reviving the dead machine. Every frame a distinct meaningful pose. The final death frame remains a fully visible recognizable D wreck. Preserve dense mechanical pixel detail, dark outlined game pixel-art and the same limited military palette, not a toy/photo/3D render. No new objects, no long beams or projectile trails.
